$comment: Known, tracked divergences between prisma/schema.prisma and the live database.
scripts/ci/check-db-drift.ts fails on any drift NOT listed here, so this file is
the reviewed record of what we are knowingly carrying and until when.
Every entry needs an owner, a reason, and an `expires` date. Past the expiry the
guard fails anyway — an allowlist without an expiry is just a permanently
disabled check, which is how the ledger reconciler ended up ignored.
Remove an entry the moment its fix lands. Do not add one to make CI green.
`enumLabelsInSchemaNotInDb` covers the OTHER direction: a label the schema has
and the database does not. That is the normal state of any pre-merge schema
PR, because the sanctioned workflow pushes the DB after merge and this guard
runs against a freshly-created rehearsal database that always lags the branch.
Without it, no PR can add an enum label at all. Same discipline as the
db-only direction — reason, tracking reference, and a SHORT expiry, because the
drift should vanish the moment `npm run db:push` runs.
`destructiveStatementsAllowed` gates `npm run db:preflight`, which runs ahead of
every `db:push`. Entries are exact `prisma migrate diff --script` statements,
whitespace-insensitive. The reset is the only occasion that should add any.

enumLabelsInSchemaNotInDb.reason: W1a (#1896) adds the consultant payout-clawback receivable. The DB push is a post-merge step in this repo's runbook, and this guard's rehearsal database is created fresh, so the enum is legitimately ahead of it for the life of the PR. A write using this label fails until `npm run db:push` runs — the clawback only writes on a lost dispute against an already-PAID ConsultantPayout, so the exposure is that path alone. Remove this entry in the same PR that runs the push.
